text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
-- S E R B I A --
- Sixth round of Yugoslav-Macedonian border talks ends; some 90 percent of the border line established.
- There is a chance for Yugoslavia to increase exports to European Union market in the second half of the year as most of the granted EU quotas have not been used yet.
- Yugoslav flag carrier got three subsidiaries Air Budva, Air Pristina and Air Beograd.

- Serbian parliament speaker and acting Serbian President Dragan Tomic called on OSCE states which normalised relations with Yugoslavia to be present at September 21 presidental and parliamentary elections.
- New terorist attacks on police patrols in ethnic Albanian Kosovo province, three wounded.
- Montenegrin electoral comission verifies Milo Djukanovic's candidacy for presidental elections in the republic called for October 5.
- Workers from Kragujevac arms plant start walking strike to Belgrade, demand payots and work.
- French Lear Liquid and German Meser and Linde interested in becoming majority share holders of Serbia's Tehnogas evaluated at 46 million German marks.
- Electric Power Industry has overhauled only 59 percent of the planned capacities in the first six months due to shortage of cash.
-- M O N T E N E G R O --

- The ruling Democratic Party of Socialists extraordinary congress called by the Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic could only be a congress of his new party, said republic's deputy prime minister Miodrag Vukovic.
- The sales of small and medium size Montenegrin firms is going according to the government's plan and 70 has been sold so far, said Mihailo Banjevic, director of the Republic's Pension Fund.

- I want to belive that the Serbian government has no intention of disrupting the unique Yugoslav market, said Montenegrin Trade Minister Branko Vujovic on frequent police, customs and financial police control on the border between the two republics.
